Proposition 21.2.8, the Banach algebra $C([a,b])$ is separable and therefore second countable
contents.reason: Separability is a property of the metric function space $C([a,b])$ itself, not of an algebra that separates points, and its proof is a countable-dense-set argument rather than an approximation-from-an-algebra argument. It belongs to the function-space-topology page this page already declares as a prerequisite; nothing in the Stone-Weierstrass development here uses or produces it.

contents.name: Proposition 21.2.9, if $\int_0^1 x^n f(x)\,dx=0$ for every natural $n$ then $f=0$
contents.reason: This moment criterion is a corollary of Weierstrass approximation, but stating it needs the Riemann integral and proving it needs the integral's linearity plus the fact that a nonzero continuous function has positive integral of its square. That integration development lives on the real-analysis integration pages, not on this topology page, so the result is recorded here for a page that has both in scope rather than dropped.

contents.name: Proposition 21.2.10, the differentiable functions on $(0,1)$ with vanishing derivative at $1/2$ are dense in $C([0,1])$
contents.reason: The witnesses in the standard proof are polynomials adjusted to have zero derivative at $1/2$, so the statement cannot even be formed without differentiability on an interval and the derivative of a polynomial. Differential calculus is developed on the real-analysis pages rather than here, so this is deferred to a page carrying both calculus and this theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 21.2.11, a necessary and sufficient condition on a closed $F\subseteq[0,\infty)$ for uniform approximation by polynomials in $x^2$
contents.reason: Erdman poses this as an open-ended exercise asking the reader to supply the condition; there is no stated result to import. Its subject is uniform approximation on a possibly noncompact closed subset of $[0,\infty)$, whereas every theorem on this page assumes a compact Hausdorff domain.

contents.name: Exercise 21.2.12, the limit of $\int_0^1x^nf(x)\,dx\big/\int_0^1x^n\,dx$ for continuous $f$ on $[0,1]$
contents.reason: This is an exercise computing a limit of integral ratios, a statement about the Riemann integral and concentration of mass near an endpoint rather than about algebras of continuous functions. It belongs with the integration pages and uses none of this page's machinery.
